message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar appears in the **"Yuppy Love"** episode of *Only Fools and Horses*. This was the first episode of **Series 6**, which originally aired on **8th January 1989** on BBC1.

In the scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool, son, nice and cool," but as he goes to lean on the bar, he doesn't notice the barman has lifted the counter hatch and falls straight through it. Trigger then looks around wondering where Del has gone.

This scene has become one of the most iconic moments in British sitcom history, frequently voted the funniest sitcom moment ever. Interestingly, it was almost different — writer John Sullivan originally wanted Del to just stumble and catch himself, but David Jason insisted on falling all the way through, based on his experience doing farces on stage. Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally meant to be in the scene; Roger Lloyd Pack apparently turned up unannounced on the shooting day and was written in, with his bemused reaction adding to the comedy.
